newsitem.title: CHINA: China stock indices end up on good sentiment.
newsitem.headline: China stock indices end up on good sentiment.

text.p: China's A and B share indices ended up on Tuesday on good sentiment and further rises are likely despite the cautiousness engendered by the corporate reporting season, brokers said.
Shanghai's B share index rose 1.206 points or 1.75 percent to 70.305 points and Shenzhen's B index gained 0.92 points or 0.59 percent to close at 157.34 points.
"Buying was quite active today, which showed confidence in China's economic prospects," a Shenzhen broker said.
"The index is likely to rise further in the coming days on follow-up buying, mainly in shares which haven't moved much over the past few days," a Shanghai broker said.
Analysts said they expected the market to maintain upward momentum over the next few days, but gains would be limited with institutions cautious in the corporate reporting season.
In Shanghai, Shanghai Lujiazui Finance and Trade Zone Development Co Ltd led the rises on institutional support, brokers said.
Lujiazui traded the most, rising $0.024 or 2.72 percent to $0.904 on volume of 2.7 million shares.
Glass maker Shanghai Yaohua Pilkington was the star on a rebound, jumping $0.032 or 7.92 percent to $0.436 on volume of 340,200 shares.

In Shenzhen, the index rose on confidence over China's economic outlook, lifted by the successful initial public offering of the Shenzhen Expressway Co's 650 million H shares in Hong Kong, brokers said.
Appliance maker Tsann Kuen was the best performer on institutional buying, advancing HK$0.15 or 3.88 percent to HK$4.02 ($0.52) on trade of 1.04 million shares.
Guangdong Provincial Expressway Development Co added HK$0.29 or 3.41 percent to HK$8.79 on volume of 244,500 shares.
Building materials producer Shenzhen Fangda traded most actively on 2.04 million shares but dropped HK$0.05 to HK$9.09 after an intraday low of HK$8.35.
Meanwhile, Shanghai's A share index rose 10.254 points or 0.89 percent to 1,160.645 points on speculative buying in selective stocks, brokers said.

Gold producer Luyin Industry Group was the star on talk of a plan to issue bonus shares, jumping 2.05 yuan or 10 percent to its limit-up of 22.50 yuan ($2.7) on volume of 2.3 million shares, brokers said.
Shenzhen's A index was up 7.82 points or 1.94 percent to 409.97 points with buying focused on stocks said to be planning good dividends, brokers said.
Chemical fibre maker Meilun Co closed the session at its 10-percent limit-up of 10.20 yuan after 4.10 million shares were traded.
